question: Can a transferable external fusion-junction oligonucleotide benchmark be built from public design-level sequences, chemistry, assay conditions, measured fusion knockdown and BOTH parent-gene effects, retaining ineffective/nonselective designs?
estimand: For each chemistry and assay stratum, design-level paired fusion and parent response at matched dose/time; data sufficiency only, no fitted prediction model.
rank_basis: Next conditional prospect after atlas deprioritization: potential experimentally anchored test of design criteria and held-out fusion utility. No paper established. PFRED/ASOG and 2015 terminal optimization defeat enumeration novelty.
success: Recover source-resolvable design/outcome evidence across at least three distinct fusion target families with multiple tested designs and nonselected/negative outcomes, enabling target-held-out validation; report actual adequacy without treating this necessary minimum as sufficient statistical power.
failure: Paired outcomes absent/selectively reported, incomparable mechanisms, or insufficient independent target families. Report recoverable subset and precise remaining lead; never infer parent sparing from viability or sequence uniqueness.
stop: One fresh worker session, medium reasoning, maximum 1800 seconds, no nested model dispatch. Bounded primary-source search and inspect most relevant studies including supplements. No manuscript or fitted benchmark. Coordinator independently verifies decisive evidence.
